basis: Cowden mucocutaneous and intestinal hamartomas and thyroid lesions are defining features; thyroid carcinoma reported in 6/7. Breast has no axis.
Umbrella for disorders associated with immunodeficiency; no specific anatomical organ is consistently affected across the group.
Defined by tongue pain or burning; tongue is gastrointestinal. Neural injury is not established by this broad symptom-defined concept.
Leukemia and congenital absence of the iris jointly define the syndrome.
Digital skeletal abnormalities and neurodevelopmental disability define FS2. Atresia annotations conflict with the explicit definition excluding GI atresia.
Acute inflammation, necrosis and hemorrhage of the exocrine pancreas.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder with progressive skeletal myopathy and defining ophthalmoplegia/ptosis; dyspnea does not establish intrinsic lung injury.
Pyramidal tract disease with frequent ataxia. Optic neuropathy in 2/2 assessed patients does not establish common ocular involvement across the 28 cases.
Benign microfollicular neoplasm arising in the thyroid gland.
Long-bone sclerosis and thickening, hypoparathyroidism with hypocalcemia, and characteristic ocular anomalies are defining syndrome features.
Inherited reflex epilepsy triggered by hot water; no other organ involvement established.
Congenital shortening and fusion abnormalities of finger and toe phalanges.
Inherited ocular coloboma with related eye malformations; unquantified extraocular findings do not establish common involvement.
Vascular telangiectases define HHT5; portal hypertension and elevated liver enzymes in 1/3 support hepatic involvement. Epistaxis reflects vascular lesions.
MYOC-associated juvenile open-angle glaucoma affects the eye and optic nerve.
Benign lesion of lymphatic vessels, classified as a cardiovascular vascular neoplasm; anatomical sites vary across subtypes.
Multiple joint contractures and pulmonary hypoplasia define the sequence. Neurological causes vary and are not universal across this umbrella.
Congenital pulmonary valve stenosis and nephrosis jointly define the disease; pulmonic stenosis is cardiac.
Clonal proliferation of hematopoietic cells; associated cardiovascular disease and leukemia are separate risks.
Congenital defect or agenesis of diaphragm muscle; impaired fetal lung growth causes pulmonary hypoplasia in most clinically significant cases.
Endocrine neoplasia and peripheral nerve neuromas of oral mucosa are defining; enteric ganglioneuromatosis is characteristic. Habitus alone adds no bone axis.
Congenital absence of the external ear, facial nerve agenesis with paralysis, and structural congenital heart disease define the syndrome.
WWOX developmental epileptic encephalopathy; retinal dysfunction on electroretinography in 7/17 (~41%) supports ocular involvement; optic atrophy is less common.
Inherited metabolic obesity; developmental/cognitive impairment and autonomic dysfunction occur in 80–99%. Hypotension does not establish intrinsic vascular damage.
Genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with universal developmental delay and EEG abnormalities; pituitary cyst in 1/6 is below threshold.
